chunks: From him, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Mas‘adah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Among what he used to do in the month of Ramadan was that he would perform supererogatory prayers every night, and he would add to the prayers he had been performing before that. From the first night until the completion of twenty nights, in every night he would pray twenty rak‘ahs: eight rak‘ahs of them after al-Maghrib, and twelve after al-‘Ishā’ al-Ākhirah. In the last ten nights, in every night he would pray thirty rak‘ahs: twelve of them after al-Maghrib, and eighteen after al-‘Ishā’ al-Ākhirah. And he would make du‘a and strive with intense exertion. He would pray one hundred rak‘ahs on the night of the twenty-first, and he would pray one hundred rak‘ahs on the night of the twenty-third, and he would strive in them both.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the night prayer after which the remaining units were performed
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset prayer, after which part of the nightly prayers were performed
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month in which these devotional acts are performed
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ ثَلَاثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ: the night of the twenty-third, singled out here for increased worship
key_terms.يَتَنَفَّلُ: he performed supererogatory prayers beyond the obligatory salat
key_terms.يَجْتَهِدُ: he exerted himself intensely in worship
key_terms.يَدْعُو: he engaged in du‘a, calling upon Allah

ai.seo_question: How many recommended prayers were performed in the nights of Ramadan, especially the twenty-first and twenty-third nights?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the pattern of recommended nightly prayers in the month of Ramadan, including additional rak‘ahs in the first twenty nights and an increased amount in the last ten nights. It also highlights special devotion, du‘a, and intensified worship on the nights of the twenty-first and twenty-third.
